title: Pre-symptomatic Alzheimer's detection and intervention windows
bottleneck: By the time Alzheimer's symptoms appear, neurodegeneration is advanced and possibly irreversible, yet reliable pre-symptomatic detection requires expensive PET scans or invasive lumbar punctures. Blood biomarkers (p-tau217 and others) are emerging, but the field does not know at what preclinical stage intervention would actually prevent decline, or whether earlier amyloid clearance would finally show benefit.
why_it_blocks: If disease-modifying drugs only work before damage is done, the entire therapeutic enterprise depends on cheap, scalable early detection plus a validated intervention window. Without both, even a perfect drug arrives too late.
current_state: Blood-based p-tau and amyloid assays are entering clinical use for diagnosis. Prevention trials in pre-symptomatic mutation carriers (DIAN) have run for over a decade; results on whether ultra-early intervention changes trajectories are still maturing.
